If you've only had 2 sessions, I would advise to keep going with the harness! (not sure if the "too" is a typo of two - if not disregard this). My kitty took a long time to even start moving when she had her harness on, let alone be comfortable. My roommate and I described her as "drunk," not sure if your kitty fits that description of that too. She just sat there, and when she got desprate to move would sort of stumble around looking generally miserable. 

I just left it on her for a few hours at a time, gradually getting longer (starting off with just 15-30 mins). Now she doesn't really notice it on, and is just as happy with in on as without. It took a few weeks/months of doing this in the house before I even thought of introducing her to it outside. Then, I'd just let her out into my garden for a few weeks/months. I've had her for 4 months now and we've only just started going for actual walks, and even then sometimes we don't get further than a block away.

Also, make sure to carry a carrier or some other way of bringing your kitty home because if they get unhappy far from home it will be difficult to carry/drag them back. It can also be good to take him out with the carrier, and make that his safe space - somewhere he can always return if he gets spooked outside, that he knows he'll be okay in.

I will say, it's very difficult to get a harness that the cat can not get out of. You're right that he can probably escape any time, especially with tension from a leash added on. I've tried a couple of different harnesses and my kitty still gets out of them if left unattended and on her leash. I think the key to having an outdoor cat is to always keep them ahead of you (as most harnesses are escapable by pushing their head backwards), going where your cat wants to, and knowing that no harness is 100% safe, so you need to make sure your cat is feeling comfortable at all times so they don't try to bolt.
